description_good.justification: README.md provides a succinct explanation of what FrugaLLM does, its architecture, and the problem it solves.

interact.justification: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md provide clear instructions on how to download, run from source, submit feedback, and participate.

contribution.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md provides step-by-step guidance on how to submit contributions and participate in the project.

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md defines explicit PR workflows, conventional commit standards, linting rules, and branch guidelines.

license_location.justification: The license is posted in a standard top-level LICENSE file in the source repository root and referenced in package.json and Cargo.toml.

floss_license.justification: FrugaLLM is released under the MIT license, a Free/Libre/Open Source Software (FLOSS) license.

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is officially approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

documentation_basics.justification: Comprehensive documentation is maintained in README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and CHANGELOG.md.

documentation_interface.justification: All IPC commands, proxy endpoints, and configuration interfaces are documented in code and architecture documentation.

discussion.justification: Public discussions and bug tracking are hosted openly on GitHub Issues and GitHub Discussions.

repo_public.justification: The source code is publicly accessible on GitHub at https://github.com/chorned/frugaLLM-App.

repo_track.justification: Full change tracking is maintained with Git version control.

repo_interim.justification: Interim changes are tracked in git feature branches and pull requests prior to release.

repo_distributed.justification: The project uses Git, a distributed version control system.

version_unique.justification: Each release is uniquely identified by a Git tag and release tag (e.g., v0.0.15).

version_semver.justification: Versions strictly adhere to Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) in package.json, Cargo.toml, and Git tags.

release_notes.justification: Human-readable release notes are maintained in CHANGELOG.md following the Keep a Changelog standard and published with every release.

report_process.justification: Issues and bug reports are submitted and tracked publicly via GitHub Issues.

report_tracker.justification: GitHub Issues provides an open, searchable defect tracker with unique issue identifiers.

report_responses.justification: SECURITY.md defines an SLA committing to acknowledge security reports within 48 hours and triage within 5 business days.

vulnerability_report_process.justification: SECURITY.md defines private disclosure channels via GitHub Security Advisories and direct security contact email hermes.horned@gmail.com.

vulnerability_report_private.justification: Private vulnerability reports are accepted via GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting and direct encrypted contact.

build.justification: The project can be cleanly built from source using standard scripts ('npm run build' and 'cargo build').

build_common_tools.justification: The build system uses standard open-source tools (Node.js, npm, Vite, Cargo, Rustc).

build_floss_tools.justification: All tools required to build the software are 100% open-source software (FLOSS).

test.justification: Automated test suites exist across the frontend (Vitest) and backend (Cargo test), totaling over 350 unit and integration tests.

test_continuous_integration.justification: Tests are automatically executed on all pull requests and commits to main via .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml.

test_policy.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly mandates that all bug fixes and new features must include automated tests.

warnings.justification: Compiler warnings and linters (TypeScript 'tsc --noEmit' and 'cargo clippy -- -D warnings') are enabled and strictly enforced.

warnings_fixed.justification: All TypeScript type errors and Cargo Clippy warnings are fixed with zero unhandled warnings.

know_secure_design.justification: Architecture enforces least privilege, prevents shell command injection by passing discrete argument arrays, and stores API keys in native OS credential keychains.

know_common_errors.justification: Defenses against common vulnerabilities (command injection, path traversal, memory unsafety) are implemented across the Rust backend and TypeScript frontend.

delivery_mitm.justification: All dependencies and release artifacts are distributed strictly over TLS/HTTPS.

delivery_unsigned.justification: Release workflows generate cryptographic SLSA build provenance attestations via actions/attest-build-provenance, and macOS binaries are Developer ID signed.

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: No known unpatched vulnerabilities older than 60 days in production code; automated security scans run weekly.

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed.justification: Zero critical vulnerabilities reported across project dependencies.

static_analysis.justification: Automated static analysis is run in CI via GitHub CodeQL, OpenSSF Scorecard, Clippy, and TypeScript.

static_analysis_fixed.justification: All static analysis findings are addressed prior to merging into main.

dynamic_analysis.justification: Playwright end-to-end integration tests run in CI on every PR, and WebdriverIO desktop smoke tests run on real packaged binaries before release.

crypto_weaknesses.justification: The project avoids implementing custom cryptography, relying solely on audited, standard system implementations (reqwest/rustls, keyring-rs).
